 Case On Regulating Private Universities Shifted From Justice Amanullah's Bench
 Amisha Shrivastava 
 18 Nov 2026 2:46 PM IST
 Share this 
 Listen to this Article The Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has shifted the Supreme Court case concerning the nationwide regulation of private universities from a division bench headed by Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah to a three-judge bench headed by Justice Vikram Nath. 
 The case, titled Ayesha Jain v. Amity University, Noida & Ors. , Writ Petition (Civil) No. 531/2025, will now be heard by a bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R. Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh. It is scheduled to be taken up on November 19.
 A bench of Justice Amanullah and Justice NV Anjaria expanded the scope of the case to address wider systemic issues. As per the latest roster, Justice Amanullah's roster does not include PIL.
 The proceedings in Ayesha Jain originally arose from an individual grievance against Amity University, Noida. The petitioner had approached the Supreme Court alleging harassment by university officials after she legally changed her name from Khushi Jain to Ayesha Jain. She alleged that the university refused to update her name in its records, resulting in her inability to fulfil the attendance requirements for examinations and the loss of an academic year.
 Although the university refunded her fees and paid her Rs. 1 lakh as compensation, the bench of Justice Amanullah and Justice NV Anjaria was dissatisfied with its conduct.
 On November 20, 2025, the bench expanded the scope of the proceedings to examine the functioning and regulatory oversight of private universities across the country in the larger public interest. 
 It sought comprehensive information from the Union Government, State Governments, Union Territories and the University Grants Commission (UGC) concerning the establishment, governance, funding and regulation of private and deemed universities.
 The bench subsequently directed the Cabinet Secretary, Chief Secretaries of States and Union Territories and the UGC Chairman to personally affirm affidavits furnishing the requisite information.
 In September 2026, the Court directed private universities across the country to disclose their audited financial statements for the preceding five years, utilisation of funds, fee structures, surplus investments and payments made to persons not directly involved in educational functions. It observed that private universities cannot be permitted to operate as profit-making institutions.
 In October 2026, the bench also took note of a purported fake medical college operating from a dilapidated farmhouse in Uttar Pradesh's Etah district, where an illiterate tea seller was allegedly shown as the institution's chairman. It directed the UGC and other regulatory authorities to issue public advisories cautioning prospective students against enrolling in institutions without verifying their authenticity.
 The case will now come before the three-judge bench led by Justice Nath.
 Case Title :  Ayesha Jain v. Amity University, Noida & Ors. Case Number :  W.P. (C) No. 531/2025 Tags
